_comment: TARGET-tier). One per crustify invocation target. Identifies the
repository root, the subdirectory crustify is scoped to (the 'target'),
the version anchor used for cache keying, and a target-local refinement
of what's out of scope. Values below illustrate a crustify run scoped to
ssl/statem inside an openssl checkout; substitute for other projects.
_comment_layout: All crustify artifacts live under a single `crustify/` directory at the
repository root (which also marks the root). REPO-ROOT-tier artifacts are
TARGET-tier artifacts live under crustify/targets/<target>/ and are
invocation-scoped: this config.json, the generated scope.json, and
per-run agent logs (logs/<session>/). repo_root and target MAY refer to
the same directory for whole-repository ports.
_comment_repo_root: Absolute path to the C/C++ project's repository root - the directory the
build system runs in and that repo-relative paths everywhere else are
interpreted against. Must exist and be a directory.
_comment_target: Repo-root-relative path to the subdirectory crustify is scoped to for
this run. Implicitly defines port scope: every source file under
Headers referenced by port-scope sources that live outside `target` are
discovered automatically by the file mapper (Phase 2); you do NOT
enumerate them here. Use `"."` to target the entire repository root.
Must exist as a directory relative to repo_root. When the port scope is a
logical SUBSET of `target` rather than a whole subdirectory, enumerate it
explicitly in `port_files` (below), which then takes precedence over this
_comment_version_anchor: Repo-root-relative path to a file whose contents identify the project
version (e.g. opensslv.h's version macro header). Used by the
library-version cache key (Phase 6 reuse layer) and for human-facing
'what version was this run against' identification. Must exist relative
_comment_port_files: OPTIONAL hand-authored port-scope file list (repo-root-relative paths).
Use it when the port scope is a logical SUBSET of `target` - a cluster of
loose files within a larger library directory - rather than a clean
subdirectory you could name in `target`. When present and non-empty, it
takes precedence over the implicit target-based scope: scope.json (v2,
entity-anchored) is the GENERATED artifact derived from this list plus
the CodeQL T1 tables, and `out_of_scope.paths` is typically left empty
because the list is already explicit. Omit the key (or leave it empty) to
fall back to the default scope = every file under `<repo_root>/<target>/`
modulo `out_of_scope.paths`. The ssl/statem values below use the implicit
subdirectory scope and so leave this empty.
_comment_out_of_scope: Target-local refinement of what crustify must NOT analyze. `paths` lists
repo-root-relative paths (directories with trailing `/` recurse; entries
without are exact-file matches) that the composer skips during T1/T2
entity discovery and edge construction, even when they fall under
via not being reachable from `target` - list them here only if
reachability would otherwise pull them in. `features` lists macro feature
names (typically `OPENSSL_NO_<FEATURE>` or equivalent) the user wants
treated as disabled; composer unions this with
